states.label: Alabama
states.notes: The state of Alabama will mail you a Voter Identificaton Card once you're registered to vote. You are *not* required to bring it to vote! Also, if you don't have a valid AL driver's license or state ID, you can't register online, but can mail in a form!

states.label: Alaska
states.notes: In Alaska, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence, parole, and probation.

states.label: Arkansas
states.notes: In Arkansas, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence, parole, and probation.

states.label: California
states.notes: In California, those convicted of felonies can register and vote after serving their sentence. Also, 16 and 17 year olds can also preregister to vote at the above link for future elections!

states.label: Colorado
states.notes: In Colorado, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence.

states.label: Connecticut
states.notes: For some reason, Connecticut's voter registration website is down every night from midnight until 6AM. So... just know that... also, in Connecticut, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence and parole.

states.label: Delaware
states.notes: The deadline for uniformed service members and Delaware citizens living out of the country is 9 days after the deadline for everyone else!

states.label: District of Columbia
states.notes: In DC, you can pre-register to vote when you're 16 years old! (You can't vote in the 2020 election, but you'll be registered for 2022 and any upcoming elections!) DC is also one of three states that lets citizens vote from prison (and/or after serving their sentence)!

states.label: Georgia
states.notes: In Georgia, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence, parole, and probation.

states.label: Hawaii
states.notes: Online registration is available through Election Day! In Hawaii, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence.

states.label: Idaho
states.notes: In Idaho, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence, parole, and probation.

states.label: Illinois
states.notes: Grace period registration is available from 27 days before through Election Day! In Illinois, those with felony convictions get their voting rights restored after serving their sentence!

states.label: Montana
states.notes: If you miss the official deadline, Montana also offers late registration up until the date before the election! Check out where you can register in the state's link above. Those with felony convictions also get their voting rights restored after serving their sentence.

states.label: Nebraska
states.notes: Listed above is the online deadline, but you can register in person through the next week! Check the state's website above for more info. Also, those with felony convictions can register and vote after serving their sentence, parole, and probation.

states.label: Nevada
states.notes: Just a heads up, the mail-in registration deadline is a few weeks earlier than the online one! Also, in Nevada, those convicted of felonies get their voting rights restored after serving their sentence.

states.label: New Hampshire
states.notes: In New Hampshire, the deadline varies between 6 and 13 days before election day depending on the town you live in (13 days is shown here, but you could have more time)! Check the state's website above for specific info. Also, in NH, those people convicted of felonies have the right to vote after serving their sentence!
